pl-l4d6c2-d1e115.summary: Asks whether those baptized by heretics must be rebaptized.

pl-l4d6c2-d1e118.summary: Answers briefly that whoever baptizes, if the form handed down by Christ is kept, gives true baptism, so the recipient must not be rebaptized.
claims: Baptism with Christ's form is true whoever gives it.
Such baptism must not be repeated.

pl-l4d6c2-d1e121.summary: Quotes Bede: whether a heretic, schismatic, or criminal baptizes confessing the Trinity, the baptized may not be rebaptized by good Catholics, lest the confession and invocation of the Trinity seem annulled.
claims: Rebaptism would annul the invocation of the Trinity.

pl-l4d6c2-d1e131.summary: Quotes Augustine: though baptism is one for heretics who baptize in the Trinity's name and for the Catholic Church, those baptized outside the Church receive it not to salvation but to ruin, having the form but denying its power; so the Church does not rebaptize them, since they were baptized in the Trinity's name, the form of the sacrament.
claims: Heretics' baptism with the Trinitarian form is the one baptism.
Outside the Church it is received to ruin, not salvation.

pl-l4d6c2-d1e140.summary: Adds Augustine: to rebaptize a heretic who received these signs of holiness is surely a sin; to rebaptize a Catholic is a most monstrous crime.
claims: Rebaptism is a sin, and of a Catholic a grave crime.

pl-l4d6c2-d1e146.summary: Concludes that those baptized even by heretics, with Christ's character preserved, are not to be rebaptized but reconciled only by the laying on of hands, to receive the Holy Spirit and as a sign of rejecting heretics.
claims: Those baptized by heretics are reconciled by the laying on of hands.

pl-l4d6c2-d1e149.summary: Notes that some doctors, like Cyprian, seem to say heretics cannot give baptism and that those said to be baptized by them must be rebaptized when they come to the Church.
claims: Cyprian and others held heretical baptism invalid.

pl-l4d6c2-d1e155.summary: Answers that this is true of those who presume to baptize outside the Church's form.
claims: Baptism outside the Church's form is invalid.

pl-l4d6c2-d1e159.summary: Admits that Cyprian seems to have strayed from truth, saying of a heretic: how can he sanctify water when he is unclean and lacks the Spirit, since whatever the unclean touches is unclean? Who can give what he does not have?
claims: Cyprian erred in holding that heretics cannot sanctify water.

pl-l4d6c2-d1e165.summary: Quotes Augustine suggesting Cyprian spoke from ignorance: so great were the merits of the glorious martyr Cyprian, who refused to recognize baptism given by heretics or schismatics in his detestation of them, that this shadow was dispelled by the light of his charity and anything needing purging was cut away by the sickle of his passion. We who recognize the truth of baptism are not thereby better than Cyprian, as we are not better than Peter because we do not compel gentiles to judaize.
claims: Cyprian's error was purged by his charity and martyrdom.
Holding the correct view does not make one better than Cyprian.

pl-l4d6c2.summary: Asks whether those baptized by heretics must be rebaptized. Whoever baptizes, if Christ's form is kept, gives true baptism, so it must not be repeated. Bede and Augustine confirm: rebaptism would seem to annul the invocation of the Trinity; heretics' baptism with the Trinitarian form is the one baptism, though received to ruin outside the Church; rebaptizing a heretic is a sin, a Catholic a monstrous crime. So those baptized by heretics with Christ's character preserved are reconciled by the laying on of hands to receive the Spirit. Cyprian and others seemed to deny heretics could baptize, which is true of those who depart from the Church's form; but Cyprian erred, asking how the unclean could sanctify water, and Augustine says the shadow was dispelled by his charity and martyrdom.
claims: Baptism given with Christ's form by anyone is true and must not be repeated.
Baptism received from heretics profits only when one returns to the Church.
Those baptized by heretics are reconciled by the laying on of hands.
Cyprian erred in denying heretical baptism, but his martyrdom purged it.
